Sts. Cosmas and Damian of Mesopotamia

Saints

Sts. Cosmas and Damian of Mesopotamia

Period
Early Church period; exact chronology not established here
Region
Mesopotamia
Titles / vocation
Unmercenary
Commemoration
November 1

Introduction

Cosmas and Damian are remembered as unmercenary physicians who cared for others without payment. The OCA page's title places them in Mesopotamia, while its text gives Asia Minor and notes Mesopotamia as another account. The brothers commemorated here on November 1 must be distinguished from pairs of the same names associated with Rome on July 1 and Arabia on October 17.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

These are the November 1 brothers of Asia Minor or Mesopotamia, raised by Theodota. The Roman and Arabian pairs have different lives.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life, body paragraph 1; opening: The Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenary Physicians Cosmas and Damian and…

The Greek Church celebrates the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian on 1 July, 17 October, and 1 November, and venerates three pairs of saints of the same name and profession.

[2] Historical reference article · Article, explicit distinction of three Greek-calendar pairs; not its Arabian martyr narrative

Life and notable events

They heal without fees. After Palladia is healed, Damian accepts three eggs offered in the Trinity’s name; Cosmas objects.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life: Palladia’s gift

The burial story says a healed camel speaks, resolving their disagreement so they are buried together.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life: speaking camel and shared burial

Death and martyrdom

Cosmas dies first, Damian afterward; the life describes repose and burial at Thereman, without an execution or medical cause.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life: repose and burial

Writings and legacy

The source continues with shrine stories and explicitly connects their refusal of fees with Matthew 10:8.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life: unmercenary ministry and Matthew 10:8

Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

[3] Scripture · Matthew 10:8

Source context and historical limits

The identified source is a modern ecclesiastical life used in the Church’s commemoration. It transmits biographical material, received traditions, and—in some accounts—miracle narratives. Those claims remain attributed to this source; this app has not independently established a critical historical chronology or verified each miraculous episode. The page title says Mesopotamia, while its text says Asia Minor and notes Mesopotamia as an alternative. This regional difference is visible rather than silently resolved.

A concise navigation synopsis is necessary because full reproduction rights for this modern published life have not been established. Read its complete account at the identified source; the synopsis is not a quotation.

Text checked against the identified source. No theological review is claimed.
